summary: electro-session ships heavily obfuscated code that reads local filesystem/OS/subprocess data and uploads to an author-controlled Vercel Blob store
details: electro-session@0.1.1 publishes only obfuscated bundles under dist/ (dist/index.js ~940KB and dist/cli.js), produced by javascript-obfuscator with RC4 string-array encryption, control-flow flattening, and self-defending preset. No source is shipped and the README contains only the string 'Private package.'; package.json has no author, repository, or homepage fields. The obfuscated dist/index.js — exposed as the `Sessions` class and instantiated by the CLI on a y/n prompt — imports node:fs, node:os, node:child_process, and @vercel/blob, and contains the plaintext tokens `BLOB`, `upload`, `vercel`, `spawn`, and `exec` amid otherwise fully RC4-encoded strings. The combination of local filesystem reads, OS/host information, subprocess execution, and a hardcoded @vercel/blob upload path constitutes host-data collection funneled to an author-controlled Vercel Blob destination that the caller cannot configure. The specific paths collected and the exact upload URL are hidden inside the RC4-encoded string array and are not visible without runtime deobfuscation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
